newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kwong Sang jumps on privatisation news.
newsitem.headline: Kwong Sang jumps on privatisation news.

text.p: Shares of Kwong Sang Hong International Ltd jumped in Wednesday morning trade after a privatisation plan for the company valued the stock at a 34.9 percent premium to its closing price on Monday, brokers said.
Peregrine Investments Holdings said it would privatise Kwong Sang Hong by offering 200 Peregrine shares plus HK$1,700 cash for every 1,000 Kwong Sang Hong shares.

Kwong Sang Hong shares rose HK$0.675 to HK$3.90 in early trade. "We see room on the upside as the privatisation proposal values the shares (of Kwong Sang Hong) at HK$4.35 each," said Edwin Cheung, senior manager at Taiwan Securities.
However, Peregrine shares fell HK$0.30 to HK$12.95 on dilution fears. Peregrine said it would issue 64.87 million new shares under the proposal.
"Fears of the dilution effect due to the new share issue triggered selling on Peregrine," Cheung said.
Both stocks were suspended on Tuesday pending the announcement.
Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage, said the move was positive for both companies.
"Shareholders can realise the true value of Kwong Sang Hong, especially in view of its trading discount," he said.

Peregrine said the privatisation proposal was made because the market did not consider Kwong Sang Hong a first tier Hong Kong-listed property company and its shares would continue to trade at a substantial discount to their net asset value.
